words.gloss: pleasingly, so that others desire to listen

literal: Speaking themselves so as to make others desire to listen, and grasping the benefit of others' words, is the principle of those who are free from blemish in excellence.
translation: To speak in a way that makes others eager to listen, and to grasp the core essence of what others say, is the practice of those who are free from flaws and rich in excellence.
modern: பிறர் விரும்பிக் கேட்குமாறு தாம் பேசி, பிறர் பேசும் சொற்களின் பயனை ஏற்றுக்கொள்வது, மாண்புகளால் குற்றமற்றவர்களின் கொள்கையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the dual nature of effective communication, which requires both eloquent expression and active listening. A skilled speaker delivers their thoughts in a pleasing manner that naturally attracts the listener's interest. At the same time, they possess the humility and wisdom to listen to others and extract the useful essence from their speech. This balanced practice of speaking agreeably and listening discerningly is the defining principle of noble minds who are free from intellectual or moral flaws.
